links.comparator_used: Standalone AI reading (same Feb 2024 cases) versus AI-assisted radiologists making the final decision
links.outcome: Fracture-level sensitivity, accuracy, specificity and PPV
links.effect: Standalone AI vs AI-assisted radiologists (Feb 2024, fracture level): sensitivity 93.5% vs 90.0% (McNemar p=0.049); accuracy 94.1% vs 93.4%; specificity 94.6% vs 96.7%; PPV 94.5% vs 96.4%; NPV 93.6% vs 90.7%. Patient-level sensitivity (p=0.871) and accuracy (p=1.000) did not differ significantly.
links.tradeoff: AI-assisted radiologists had lower sensitivity, so subtle fractures flagged by the AI may have been overlooked. AI use was discretionary and not recorded, which introduces reader and confirmation bias.
links.quote: In conclusion, this study demonstrates that a standalone AI system achieves high diagnostic performance in musculoskeletal trauma imaging, often statistically outperforming AI-assisted radiologists in both sensitivity and accuracy.

design_hint: discretionary AI-assisted radiologist reading vs. no AI access
